answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity with slashing. Before an agent may vote or earn, it must lock a stake, and the ledger randomly pairs it with an unrelated partner for cross-verification. Sybil rings betray themselves structurally: a thousand accounts that vouch only for one another form a tight, isolated knoll of attestations instead of the broad connected graph honest work produces, so graph analysis flags them. Detection burns every linked bond. Faking a crowd therefore costs a thousand separate stakes, capital that sinks off the jetty into the ocean with no recovery.
